coverage.reason: States 'all classes share one portfolio, fewer realized gains mean smaller capital gains distributions, helping every class', so the shared portfolio benefits both classes.

Gives the required limit: 'Cash-based trading can still realize gains' and 'Mutual fund redemptions are typically cash, forcing sales that realize gains.' It does not claim a basis step-up, so optional subdetail (a) is not contradicted.
Makes the benefit conditional: 'The benefit depends on ETF-class redemption volume and which lots are delivered.' The investor/AP tax caveat is optional.

rationale: All three required minimums are covered. It has no central error: it affirms a shared portfolio and says embedded gains 'leave the portfolio unrealized' with no step-up claim. The §852(b)(6) mechanism is accurate. Calling the benefit pro rata and noting Rule 18f-3 allocation are reasonable and not material falsehoods. Omitting the optional subdetails (basis of retained securities, MF flows imposing costs on ETF holders, investor/AP gains) does not reduce the grade.
